subject: ACME POC Kickoff Recap & Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: ACME POC Kickoff Recap & Next Steps

Tom / Priya — thanks again for a productive kickoff this morning. Below is a concise recap, confirmed scope, success metrics, owners, and immediate next steps so we all have the same understanding. I attached the kickoff agenda and the POC scope spreadsheet for reference.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent customer response time from current NLU pipeline (latency spikes during peak)
- Manual prompt tuning and frequent regressions across feature sets
- High per-request cost on current managed solution for our expected volume

POC goals (6 weeks):
1) Reduce tail latency for customer-facing chat flows to <= 400ms P95 for 512-token average exchanges.
2) Demonstrate a 30% reduction in per-1000-token cost vs current baseline (benchmark will be provided by ACME).
3) Ship a stable prompt set + eval harness that keeps semantic accuracy within +/- 2% of current model while lowering cost.

Scope / Deliverables (what Redwood will provide):
- Deployment of model variant (quantized) in a dedicated sandbox instance for ACME.
- Shared eval harness (prompt set + metrics dashboard) to run nightly regressions.
- Access and onboarding checklist for engineers (service account, API keys, sample prompts).
- Weekly syncs + one interim mid-POC quality review.

Success metrics and monitoring:
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 reported per route (target P95 <= 400ms).
- Cost: $ per 1k tokens baseline vs POC (target -30%).
- Quality: Semantic similarity + regression tests on the provided prompt set (target within +/- 2%).

Owners / Contacts:
- ACME: Tom Reyes (product lead), Priya Sharma (ML engineer), Sanjay Patel (infra)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (eng. lead / sales TL) - marissa.cole@redwood.ai; Aditya Rao (solutions engineer) - aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): access provisioning, sample data & prompt set shared by ACME, Redwood sandbox created.
- Week 1: baseline benchmarks and initial prompt tuning.
- Week 2-4: iterative tuning, nightly evals, performance optimizations (batching, KV caching).
- Week 5: stability & regression sweep.
- Week 6: final report + recommendations for production roll.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- ACME: Share baseline cost numbers and 10k representative prompts by EOD Mon (Priya).
- ACME: Provide VPN/SSH or service account access details for sandbox (Sanjay).
- Redwood: Provision sandbox and create service account + API key by Tue COB (Marissa / Aditya).
- Redwood: Share initial prompt/eval template and Nightly-eval dashboard link by Wed (Marissa).

If this matches your view, please reply with any corrections and confirm dates for the sample data and access.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly right and clear. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline numbers: we'll export last 30 days of token usage and current spend; Priya will share this by EOD Monday (11/16).
- Prompts: Priya has a curated list of ~12 canonical prompts and we can add 8-10 edge cases for regressions. Will deliver as CSV.
- Access: Sanjay prefers a temporary service account with scoped API keys rather than VPN if Redwood supports it (easier for us to audit). If we need VPN for deeper infra checks, we'll coordinate separately.

One internal ask: can Redwood confirm the quantization profile you plan to use and whether there will be any differences in output tokens (determinism) we should expect? We want to understand potential delta in exact tokenization/outputs for legal/regulatory logging.

Also copying our UX PM (Ben Carter) in case we need to align on UX test cases next week.

Tom — great, thanks for the quick confirmations and the preferred access model. A few quick answers and clarifications below: 

Quantization / determinism:
- We'll use the 4-bit quantized variant (q4_0) for the initial POC to hit the cost targets while preserving semantic fidelity. In our prior benchmarks q4_0 keeps mean semantic similarity >98% vs float baseline; we will include a deterministic seed workflow for evals so you can reproduce outputs for logging. There can be small tokenization differences; we will surface a token-diff report as part of the nightly evals.

Service account approach (recommended):
- Redwood can provision scoped service accounts with short-lived API keys. We'll send the onboarding email with instructions for rotating keys and least-privilege roles. Sanjay, please confirm preferred key rotation cadence (we can default to 7 days for the POC).

Prompt set / evals:
- Please upload the CSV of canonical + edge prompts to the Drive link below (or reply with the file). Our eval harness will run nightly, producing: semantic-similarity, slot-filling accuracy, and regression flags. We'll surface failing prompts in the dashboard and propose tuning suggestions.

Initial deliverables & dates (updated):
- Mon 11/16: ACME -> Baseline cost export + prompt CSV (Priya).
- Tue 11/17: Redwood -> Sandbox provisioned, service account + API key emailed (Marissa/Aditya).
- Wed 11/18: Redwood -> First baseline benchmark + nightly-eval template link.
- Weekly syncs: Fridays 10am PT, starting 11/20 (invite to follow).

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Priya: upload prompt CSV + baseline export by 11/16 (Priya).
- Sanjay: confirm key rotation cadence and whether you need VPN for infra-level tests by 11/16.
- Marissa / Aditya: provision sandbox and share credentials by 11/17.

I'll create the shared Drive folder and add the eval template tonight. Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ABCDEFghIjKlmnoPQRs

Let me know if anything else should be included. Otherwise, we'll proceed on the timeline above.

Thanks —
Marissa

Adding a quick internal note — happy to own the sandbox provisioning and the onboarding checklist. I'll run the initial benchmark once I have the prompt CSV and baseline export. A few engineering notes for ACME to consider that will speed things up: 

- Throughput expectations: if you expect sustained ~100 rps across chat endpoints, we should configure 2x the initial capacity to account for variance during tuning. Please indicate target RPS in your baseline export.
- Logging / telemetry: We'll provide structured logs and a short token-diff report as Marissa described. If you need logs shipped to your Splunk/Datadog, send ingestion endpoint + API token and we'll wire it up in the sandbox.
- Attachments: onboarding_checklist.pdf (contains step-by-step for service accounts, key rotation, and sample curl POSTs).

I'll provision the sandbox today and email credentials to Tom and Sanjay once ready. If there are any firewall rules needed for outbound requests from our sandbox to your logging endpoints, please send them to me.
